not_rules.quote: Post-nominals and titles of status show the awards and honours an individual has. List them in the correct order.
Post-nominals are the shortened forms for academic awards and civil and military honours.

not_rules.note: Lead-in phrase introducing the negative rules on full stops, spaces, and commas.

covers.quote: There is an order in which to write the post-nominals.
In summary, the rule is to write the highest honour first. The order is:
King’s Counsel (KC) or Senior Counsel (SC) or Justice of the Peace (JP)

parts.quote: The Hon Ken Wyatt AM MP

rules.quote: Use post-nominals in the correct order
rules.specification: List post-nominals in the order: (1) honours and awards, (2) King's Counsel (KC), Senior Counsel (SC), or Justice of the Peace (JP), (3) university degrees and diplomas, (4) membership of professional associations, (5) membership of parliament.
rules.violation_condition: post-nominals listed out of sequence according to the hierarchy of honours/awards, legal appointments, academic qualifications, professional associations, and parliamentary membership
when: Applying to post-nominals following a person's name.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: Heading is the primary rule statement, with list items specifying the required order.

examples.note: AM and FAHMS written without interior full stops or spaces.

rules.quote: full stops or spaces within post-nominals
rules.violation_condition: use of full stops or spaces within an individual post-nominal (e.g. 'A.M.' or 'Ph. D.')
rules.why: Specific punctuation and spacing prohibition for post-nominals under 'Don't use'.

examples.note: No commas between Wood, AM, and FAHMS.
No commas between Wyatt, AM, and MP.

parts.quote: The Hon Ken Wyatt AM MP

rules.violation_condition: use of a comma before a post-nominal or between multiple post-nominals

covers.quote: Vice-regal and ecclesiastical titles and Australian Defence Force ranks usually precede all other titles.
Follow these with any other titles (such as ‘Dame’, ‘Sir’ and ‘Dr’) immediately before a person’s name.

examples.note: His Excellency and General precede the Honourable and the personal name.

parts.quote: His Excellency General the Honourable David Hurley AC DSC (Retd)

examples.note: Ecclesiastical title (The Right Reverend) precedes other title (Dr).

parts.quote: The Right Reverend Dr Sarah Macneil
General Sir John Wilton KBE CB DSO

rules.quote: Write titles before a person’s name in the correct order
rules.specification: Vice-regal and ecclesiastical titles and Australian Defence Force ranks precede other titles, which in turn immediately precede the person's name.
rules.violation_condition: titles preceding a person's name placed in an incorrect sequence (e.g. placing titles like Dame/Sir/Dr ahead of vice-regal, ecclesiastical, or ADF titles)
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: The heading states the overarching rule, while the following two paragraphs detail the exact relative sequence.
